tool_input.content:
---
name: zspec-program-lessons
description: Lessons from the 2026-09-20 Z-spec gap program (PR #530) — spec-first finds bugs, records rot, toolchain traps
metadata:
  type: project
---

PR #530 (merged 2026-09-20) delivered four Z specs + a fuzz gate. Durable
lessons:

1. Writing enforcement claims as checkable models found counter-examples
   for three live bugs and one unknown bug (ethos-fhns: Store.Update can
   reopen a closed mission). Spec-first is the repo's proven bug-finder.
2. ethos-015a is structural: git worktree remove is unobservable to
   ethos, so only a per-machine spool satisfies audit durability —
   formal basis for [[ethos-ss2x]] (SQLite bead).
3. Recorded claims rot without mechanical re-derivation — tests written
   from implementations pinned bugs as correct; the fresh specs repeated
   the same failure (non-reproducing ProB counts, a dead clause).
   Independent evaluator re-runs are mandatory for verification work.
4. Toolchain traps (documented in the specs): fuzz does not compile
   LaTeX; safety properties baked into the checked type are
   unfalsifiable (errata technique: decoupled variants); under-
   constrained axioms multiply ProB witnesses; deadlock/goal-search
   counts are search-order artifacts — only verdicts reproduce.
5. Cost calibration: the whole program was one working day (5 missions,
   27 findings closed) against a month producing ~40 bugs in the same
   subsystems.

**Why:** operator asked "what did we learn"; these generalize beyond the PR.

**How to apply:** before fixing enforcement/lifecycle bugs, check for a
spec (docs/spec-*.tex) and implement against it; lifecycle PRs must
amend spec-mission-lifecycle.tex or state why not (checklist rule);
never trust recorded tool counts without a re-run.
